question: A release pipeline calls claude -p --output-format json "summarize the changes in this release" and pipes the result to a script that reads .result. Finance now also wants each invocation's per-model API spend recorded for cost tracking, without adding any new flags. Where does that information already appear?
options: A) The cost data is only available by separately querying the Claude usage dashboard after the run completes
B) Cost data only appears when --output-format stream-json and --verbose are both set, so the job must switch formats
C) Per-invocation cost is written to a local .claude/usage.log file that the script must additionally parse
D) The JSON response body already includes total_cost_usd along with a per-model cost breakdown alongside the result field
correct_answers: D) The JSON response body already includes total_cost_usd along with a per-model cost breakdown alongside the result field
explanations: The usage dashboard is a separate aggregate view; per-invocation cost is already returned inline in the JSON response, so a dashboard lookup isn't required for this use case.
Cost fields are part of the standard --output-format json response; switching to stream-json is unnecessary and changes the output shape the script already depends on.
Claude Code does not write per-invocation cost to a local usage.log file; the cost fields are part of the JSON response returned directly by the CLI.

Correct. With --output-format json, the response payload includes total_cost_usd and a per-model cost breakdown, so scripted callers can track spend per invocation directly from the existing JSON output.
